_about: CONTENT [twenty-five things on the road], 11/2/26 (Paolo 11/2: 'I want more content for the game, more content'; earlier: 'it got pretty boring... a little more quests to do'). THE ROAD'S EVENTS, Battle Brothers' way (reference/library/battle_brothers/: an event stops the company on the road, a face and a situation, two or three choices, a real cost or gain; some remember what you chose and come back later). A modder's file: every event is a row; slices/bohemia_road_events.js reads it and owns no words of its own. WHO: a name and a portrait look (engine/bohemia_crew_faces.js LOOKS: cast_* and faction_*). WHERE: any | paved (the five asphalt road kinds) | rough (rail bed, dry wash) | a district id. WHEN: day | night | any. NEEDS: flag / notflag (a chain), min_day, bats (he must have that many for the event to come), men (crew at least). OPTS: two or three; each option's fx is what happens: bats (+/-), food (+/- a man's night each, the wagon's), gear (a weapon id from records/target/bb/weapons.json, or -1 to lose the bag's newest item), man (+1 joins with {name, look, bg}; -1 one walks), mood ({act, place}: act from records/target/bb/relations.json, place 'near' = the nearest town, or 'faction:<word>'), mins (the clock), flag / unflag (chains), fight ({foe, n, label, win, lose}), chance ({p, yes, no}), quest (a side quest id in BOHEMIA_SIDE_QUESTS.json), say (the speaker's answer). need: what an option asks before it can be chosen. Every word is an attempt, draft:true; the valley's people talk Spanglish, the player's choices are plain English (THE FIRST VOTES: the player does not speak Spanglish). Numbers are shapes TUNING owns. CONTENT 2 (11/3, ask line 342): sixteen more (fifteen and one payoff), eleven of them using what is new on the map: WHERE 'pass' (the mountains' pass roads, a block with passRoad); NEEDS party ({agenda: caravan | crew | patrol, faction?, within}: a roaming party on the map that near), raided (a crew walking home from somebody's ground, the raided town), boss_sign (a boss's sign standing in the world); the words carry {party} {toward} {raided} {raider} {boss} {town}, filled from what the map says ({word|what to say if it has none}); a man who joins can come wearing gear (man.gear: the cell vest's hire, gear.acc).

director.why: Battle Brothers fires a road event every so often on the march, rarely back to back, never in the first moments. Here: never in the first real minute of play (THE SECOND VOTES: nothing happens in the first second; the overworld law: never in the first minute), at least 22 blocks walked since the last one, then a 6% chance each block (about 38 blocks between events on average, two to four an in-game day of steady walking). An event already met waits three in-game days before it can come again (his repeat ruling, 9/5); a chain's events come once.

more_about: WORLD 14 (11/10, VAMILY rule 443(b)): twelve more rows, each with 'lane' WORLD 14 and its Battle Brothers 'kind' (company: his own men; location: the road). New words a row may use, read by slices/bohemia_road_more.js through the seam in slices/bohemia_road_events.js: needs.crew {n: 1 or 2, bg: [trades]} (one or two of HIS men, never YOU: {man}, {man_look}, {man_bg}, {other}, {other_look}; the speaker may be his own man, who.name '{man}'); needs.place {hidden: true} (a real place of records/target/bb/real_places.json still under the fog: {place}, {place_id}, {blocks}); fx.wound {name, hp} (that man loses the hitpoints, kept by the company's condition record, mended by the clock and the camp); fx.leaves {name} (he leaves the company); fx.open {id} (the place's fog lifts and it is named on the map); 'head' the card's top line. Written by tools/bohemia_world14_road_events_data.py; gate gates/twelve_more_on_the_road_gate.js. 11/11, twelve more (his place, the bosses, his jobs): needs.home {planted: true} or {} ({home}, {home_blocks}); needs.boss {sign | found | fallen} ({boss}, {boss_place}, {boss_blocks}); needs.job {held: true} ({job}, {job_from}, {job_pay}); fx.home {kind, name, build | look | gives | says} (a gift to his place through HOME BASE's own seam; it waits until he plants); fx.boss {find: true} (the boss's sign read: found, his place out of the dark). Gate gates/the_road_knows_his_place_gate.js. 11/14, twelve that follow from what he did: needs.boss {fallen} after a boss he put down; needs.deed {failed} or {helped} ({deed_town}: a town where he failed a job, or finished one or did it a favour, within 14 days, kept by slices/bohemia_road_more.js from the jobs' own settled acts).

who.name: A KID WITH A CAN
who.from: on the shoulder

events.says: Oye, jefe. Two days no food. I don't want batteries, just something to eat. My brother says ask the ones with guns, they got food.

opts.t: Give him two nights of food.

fx.say: Gracias. I don't forget faces. Neither does my brother.
Five. Okay. That's a can at the post. Gracias, jefe.
Sí. Everybody keeps walking.

who.name: THE KID'S BROTHER
who.from: waiting by a burned car

events.says: You fed my little brother. So I tell you straight: three men sit on the next bend with a rifle. I know a way around. And if you want, I walk with you.

fx.say: Teo. I carry, I watch, I don't complain. Vámonos.
Through the culvert. And there is a dead man's pack down there. Six batteries. Yours.
Your call, jefe. Watch the bend.

who.name: DOÑA PILI
who.from: under a truck with no front wheel

events.says: The axle, mijo. I got the part, I don't got the arms. One hour of your boys lifting and I owe you. A trucker always pays back, ask anybody.

fx.say: Ándale, that's it. I run the Primm road. You'll see me again.

opts.t: Sell her the time: ten batteries.

fx.say: Ten. Pues, fair. Nobody lifts for free no more.
Nobody has time. That's why the trucks stopped.

who.name: DOÑA PILI
who.from: her truck, running

events.says: ¡Mira quién es! The arms! I been looking for you. A crate of beans fell off the back of my own truck, if you understand me.

fx.say: Six nights for your boys. We're square. Until next time.
Twenty-five, and don't tell my husband.

who.name: A DRONE IN THE DIRT
who.from: one rotor still spinning

events.says: (a delivery drone, face-down, its little speaker looping) Paquete en camino. Package on its way. Paquete en camino. The box under it is sealed with the Network's tape.

fx.say: Paquete... en... (the speaker dies. Eighteen batteries in foam, packed like eggs.)

opts.t: Carry it to the nearest town.

fx.say: Gracias por su entrega. Thank you for your delivery. (somebody, somewhere, logged your face.)
Paquete en camino. Paquete en camino.

who.name: NETWORK COURIER
who.from: two drones over his head

events.says: Every drone has a camera, amigo. We saw you open our box. You give back eighteen and a little for the trouble, or my friends here come down.

fx.say: Smart. The Network forgets fast when it's paid.

win.say: They dropped their own batteries running.

lose.say: They took fifteen and the drone's camera kept rolling.

who.name: NETWORK COURIER
who.from: leaning on a dead streetlight

events.says: You the one who walked our drone home? Honest people are rare as rain. The Network pays honest. Here.

fx.say: Twenty. And your name is good on our wire now.
News? The Reds move water on the night of the full moon. And eight batteries, because I like you.

who.name: LA TOLLKEEPER
who.from: a shopping cart across the road

events.says: This road is ours today, my loves. Five batteries a head, or ten for all of you because you dress so ugly I feel sorry. Rick Owens would cry.

fx.say: Gracias, gorgeous. Next time you pass, you pass free.

opts.t: Push the cart out of the way.

win.say: The cart had their whole day's take in it.

lose.say: They took the ten anyway, and your hat.

fx.say: Long way is free. Long way is also long.

who.name: LA TOLLKEEPER
who.from: the cart, now with a parasol

events.says: My ugly friends who pay! Go, go, free road. And a gift: the men at the overpass are new and scared. Scared men sell cheap.

fx.say: And five back, because I'm in a mood. Don't get used to it.

opts.t: Buy food off the overpass men.

fx.say: Five nights of food for eight. Told you. Scared.

who.name: A MAN ON A MATTRESS
who.from: under an overpass

events.says: Fever three days. My wife went for the clinic, she don't come back. If you got water, a little. If you don't, then just tell her I waited.

opts.t: Leave him a night of food and water.

fx.say: Dios te lo pague. Her name is Lupe. Lupe Ortiz.

opts.t: Carry him to the nearest town.

fx.say: You carried a stranger. People there saw you do it.
I'll tell her a group came by. That's something.

who.name: LUPE ORTIZ
who.from: running down the road

events.says: You're them. He told me. He lived, ¿me oyes? He lived. I got nothing much. I sew. Let me give you something I sewed.

fx.say: A knife, in a sheath I stitched with his old belt. Cut good things with it.
Then I tell everybody in town what you did. That's worth more, maybe.

who.name: A CROW ON A BODY
who.from: the ditch

events.says: (a courier, two days dead, still holding the strap of a bag. The bag has a Remnants seal. A crow looks at you like you're next in line.)

fx.say: Fourteen batteries and a letter nobody will get now. The Remnants count their bags.
The crow waits on a sign the whole time. It does not like you.
The crow goes back to work.

who.name: MADAME BOTTEGA
who.from: a rack of clothes in the road

events.says: Darling. The world ended and you still dress like a parking lot. One coat, Balenciaga, real, from the Forum Shops. Twenty batteries and you live forever.

opts.t: Buy something cheaper: a knife she keeps under the rack.

fx.say: The knife. Tragic. But it matches nothing, so it matches everything.

opts.t: Trade her two nights of food.

fx.say: Food! Fashion eats too, my love. Six batteries and my blessing.
Nobody buys today. Everybody dies ugly.

who.name: A BOY WITH A SLING
who.from: on a car roof

events.says: Coyotes, big ones, the lab kind. They follow you since the wash. Gimme three batteries and I show you where they sleep. You kill them, the skins sell.

win.say: Skins for fifteen batteries at the post, and meat for two nights.

lose.say: They got into the wagon on the way out.

fx.say: Okay. They're still following you, though.

who.name: HERMANO CANDELARIO
who.from: a milk crate pulpit

events.says: The dollar was a false god and it died like one. Now everybody worships the battery. Brothers, give one battery to the Church, and the Church remembers your face at the gate.

fx.say: Five. Bendito. The sisters will hear your name tonight.
...and on the eighth day the screens went dark and man looked up. Gracias for listening. Nobody listens.
Walk, then. The road listens.

who.name: A WOMAN WITH TWO JUGS
who.from: running from a pump house

events.says: ¡Ayúdame! They say I steal the water, but it's my pump, my father dug it! They're coming. Hide me in your wagon, please.

yes.say: They walk right past. She leaves you three jugs. Three nights of water.

win.say: She gives you the jugs anyway. Her father's pump is hers again tonight.

lose.say: They took her and two of your jugs.

opts.t: Turn her in for the reward.

fx.say: Twelve batteries from the pump men. She doesn't look at you once.
She runs on into the dark.

who.name: A RADIO ON A POLE
who.from: tied with wire, at head height

events.says: (a radio taped to a pole, playing a weather report from before. Sunny. Seventy-two. The dollar is up. Then the same report again. Somebody has been changing its batteries.)

fx.say: Four batteries. The report stops on 'the dollar is'. The quiet is worse.
Sunny. Seventy-two. The dollar is up.

who.name: THE MAN WHO CHANGES THEM
who.from: behind the pole

events.says: You took the batteries out of my radio. My wife recorded that report the morning before. It's the last of her voice. Put four back or I follow you forever.

fx.say: Eight. She'll talk for two more weeks. Gracias. Go with God.

fight.label: the radio man and his son

win.say: He doesn't follow you. But you hear the report in your head all night.

lose.say: He takes ten and walks back to his pole.

who.name: TWO RED DESERTERS
who.from: red bandanas in their pockets

events.says: We quit the Reds. They make us shoot water thieves, kids, everybody. We fight good. Take us, or don't, but don't tell the Reds you saw us.

fx.say: Benny. The other one goes his own way. The Reds will hear, they always hear.

opts.t: Turn them in to the Reds.

fx.say: Twenty batteries from a Red patrol. The two boys don't fight it.
Gracias. We were never here.

who.name: AN OLD DEALER
who.from: a card table on the median

events.says: One hand, high card. You win, I give you twenty. You lose, I take ten. The house always won, mijo. The house is dead now. Let's see.

yes.say: King. Ay, the king. Take it before I change my mind.

no.say: Seven. Bad night for sevens. Gracias.

opts.t: Ask him about the old Strip.

fx.say: The lights were on twenty-four hours. Nobody looked up. Now everybody looks up. Go on.

who.name: A BRIDE IN SILVER
who.from: a wedding in a parking lot

events.says: ¡Vengan, vengan! A wedding! Two families stop fighting today. Eat, drink, and if you have a gift, the gift table is the truck bed.

fx.say: Ten! You eat like family. Take a plate for the road. The whole town will hear.
Eat, eat. Nobody counts at a wedding. Well. My aunt counts.
Next time, then. There's always a next wedding. Or a funeral.

who.name: A HUNTER WITH ONE ARM
who.from: a blind made of doors

events.says: Lab cat. American lion, they said, from a bone in Tule Springs. It took my arm and my partner. It sleeps in the wash. Kill it and the reward is yours, I only want to see it dead.

win.say: Thirty batteries, my whole savings. He cries like a kid. Gracias.

lose.say: It's still out there. It knows you now.

fx.say: It will be. It's always everybody's fight, later.

who.name: A SCRAPPER
who.from: knee-deep in a dead car

events.says: Good copper in this one, but I need four hands. You help me pull it, we split it. Hour of work. Trades rules, half and half.

fx.say: Half and half, ten each. The Trades will hear you work clean.
¡Rata! I know your faces! The whole Trades will know them!
Pues, more for me.

who.name: A WOMAN IN A WHITE COAT
who.from: walking toward you, slowly

events.says: Don't be scared. I'm a nurse, I walk at night because the days are too hot. I have bandages and nobody to give them to. Can I walk with you to the next town?

opts.t: Walk her to the next town.

fx.say: Thank you. I'll tell the Volunteers who walked me. We look after the ones who look after us.
Bandages, eight batteries' worth at any post. A fair trade at night.

who.name: A GIRL IN A STORM DRAIN
who.from: her voice, under the street

events.says: ¡Aquí abajo! My foot is stuck in the grate. The water comes when it rains, and it's going to rain. Please.

fx.say: She runs home without saying gracias. Later the whole town knows who did it.

yes.say: She's out. Scraped up, but out. Gracias, gracias.

no.say: It doesn't give. You dig anyway. Forty-five minutes.

who.name: CARTEL CHECKPOINT
who.from: two trucks across the road

events.says: Inspección. What's in the wagon, jefe? We take a tenth of everything, it's the law now. Our law. Or you can try to argue.

fx.say: Eight batteries and a night of food. Pásale. Have a nice day.

yes.say: The jefe laughs. 'You got balls. Go.' Nobody pays.

win.say: Their cash box. Twenty-five. The cartel will want it back.

lose.say: They take twenty and the long way of making a point.

fx.say: Long way around. Smart, maybe.

who.name: A THREE-LEGGED DOG
who.from: and its owner, a very old man

events.says: Chato smells water. Four legs, three legs, he smells it better than any machine. Two batteries and he finds you a cistern nobody knows.

opts.t: Pay two and follow the dog.

fx.say: A cistern under a gas station. Four nights of clean water. Chato wants a scratch.
He likes you. Chato likes everybody. That's his problem.

who.name: THE SMILING MAN
who.from: standing very still in the middle of the road

events.says: (he holds a TV with no back. On it, your own crew, walking this road, from above, ten minutes ago. He smiles.) Everything is recorded. Do you want to see what happens next?

yes.say: Static. Then a picture of a cache under a billboard. It's real. Ten batteries.

no.say: Static. When you look up he's gone, and so are two nights of food from the wagon.

fx.say: He turns his head to follow you. Just his head.

who.name: BLUES SERGEANT
who.from: a patrol of four

events.says: Raiders hit a farm west of here. We're short a gun. Ride with us one hour, the Blues pay what's fair, and we don't forget who stood with us.

win.say: Twenty batteries and a handshake. The Blues remember.

lose.say: The raiders got away. The sergeant doesn't blame you. Much.

fx.say: Busy. Everybody's busy until it's their farm.

who.name: EL VAQUERO
who.from: a rancher with a coiled bullwhip on his shoulder

events.says: Mi patrón's ranch out by Moapa is dust. The cattle went when the feed trucks stopped coming. All I got left is this. A rodeo bullwhip, braided by hand. It cracks louder than a pistol and it don't need bullets. Sixty batteries. In town they want a hundred.

fx.say: Take care of it. It took my abuelo a whole winter.

opts.t: Trade him four nights of food for it.

fx.say: Food. Okay. Food I can't braid. It's yours.
Sí. Nobody needs a cowboy in a city with no cows.

who.name: A KID WITH A CUE
who.from: outside a pool hall with the windows out

events.says: The Golden Cue closed forever, so we make spears out of the cues. Two cues taped long, a knife on the tip. It reaches two houses, jefe, it keeps a dog off you. Twelve batteries. In the market it's seventeen.

fx.say: Hold it at the back, not the middle. The middle is for the felt.
Four for the tape and the blade. Your tape job is ugly, but it holds.
Okay. The dogs don't care how cool you look.

who.name: CHISPA
who.from: a thin man in a vest stitched with salvaged cells, a switch in his fist

events.says: Nobody hires me. They see the vest and cross the street. Mira, I'm not crazy. Four cells wired to a switch. If I go down, the switch lets go, and whoever is standing on me goes with me. You want a man nobody wants to get close to? Twelve batteries and I walk with you.

fx.say: Bueno. Walk in front of me, not behind. Everybody learns that the first day.

opts.t: Feed him and send him home.

fx.say: Home. Sí. I'll eat first and think about home after.
Like everybody. It's okay. I'm used to the street.

who.name: A CARAVANS DRIVER
who.from: a box truck on three wheels, the stencil on its door

events.says: Ey! The {party} delivery to {toward|the next town}, that's us. The axle went. The rest of the convoy is up the road, they don't stop, that's the rule. I got medicine in the back and two guys with bats for a whole valley. Help me push it to the convoy and they pay you, I swear on my mother.

opts.t: Push the truck to the convoy.

fx.say: Eighteen, from the convoy boss. He didn't say thank you. He never does.

win.say: Antibiotics and a box of crackers. The {party} will hear about this.

lose.say: Two guys with bats. You were wrong about them.

fx.say: Sí. The convoy left us too.

who.name: EL FLACO RUIZ
who.from: lying flat in the creosote with two others and a rifle

events.says: Shh. Get down. That's the {party} convoy coming, to {toward|wherever}. We hit it at the bend. You want a share? Hold the back, nobody gets hurt that matters.

win.say: Your share is thirty-four. Ruiz counts it twice, slow, so you can see.

lose.say: The guards were ready. Ruiz ran first.

opts.t: Walk up and warn the convoy.

fx.say: The convoy boss pays twelve for the warning. Ruiz saw your face.
Smart. You never saw me.

who.name: EL FLACO RUIZ
who.from: on the road ahead, waiting for you this time

events.says: You. The one who warned the {party}. Two of my guys are in their pen now because of you. I'm not here to kill you, I'm here for what they cost me. Twenty.

fx.say: Twenty. Now we're nothing to each other. That's the best thing I can be.

win.say: He had ten on him and a photo of a dog.

lose.say: He took twelve and your hat.

opts.t: Tell him to take it up with the convoy.

fx.say: Ja. With the {party}. Okay, jefe. You're funny. I'll be around.

who.name: THE STONE MAN
who.from: stacking stones at the top of the pass

events.says: Count the stones, amigo. One for every car that tried the pass after the dollar went. Fifty-one. The ones that made it don't get a stone. Leave a battery on the pile and you make it down. Everybody who left one made it down. I counted them too.

opts.t: Leave a battery on the pile.

fx.say: Bueno. Keep left at the burned bus. Right goes to the drop.

opts.t: Take the batteries off the pile.

yes.say: Nothing happens. The wind comes up the pass and the stone man doesn't look at you again.

fight.label: the coyotes that live under the pass

win.say: Two coyotes, thin as wire. The stone man adds two stones.

lose.say: You drop the batteries running. The pile gets them back.

fx.say: Fifty-one. I'll leave room for one more.

who.name: LA CHOFER
who.from: a school bus full of people, stopped on the pass road, its brakes smoking

events.says: We're going over to Pahrump. My cousin says there's well water there and nobody counts it. Thirty-two people. The brakes are cooked from the grade and the next part is down. You got a man who knows brakes? We pay what we have.

opts.t: Lend them a man for two hours.

fx.say: Twelve batteries and two bags of tortillas. Thirty-two people wave at you out the back window.

opts.t: Sell them two nights of food.

fx.say: Fourteen. They needed brakes more than food, but okay.
Okay. We'll go slow. Pray for the slow.

who.name: A MAN WITH A RADIO
who.from: a rope across the pass road, a rockslide behind it

events.says: The pass is ours. Nobody else clears the rockslides, so everybody pays the rock tax. Five. Or pick up a shovel, we got a slide right there, two hours and you walk free.

fx.say: Five. Mutual aid, compa. The rocks don't care who's in charge.

opts.t: Dig the slide for two hours.

fx.say: You dig. They pay you four for the extra rocks. Nobody owns this pass and everybody works it.

win.say: Fifteen in their tax box. The slide is still there.

lose.say: They take ten and your shovel would have been cheaper.

who.name: DOÑA LUPE
who.from: pulling a wagon of everything she owns, out of the {raided} town

events.says: The {raider} hit the {raided} town last night. They took the water, the cells, my cousin's truck. They're walking home with it right now, you can see their dust. Me, I'm going to my sister. You got a little food for the road?

opts.t: Give her two nights of food.

fx.say: Que Dios te lo pague. Everybody from the {raided} town remembers the ones who gave.

opts.t: Go after the crew and the truck.

fight.label: the {raider} crew, walking home with it

win.say: Twenty-eight batteries off their backs, and the truck. Lupe's cousin comes for it on foot.

lose.say: There were more of them than dust. You got out.

fx.say: Sí. Everybody's walking today.

who.name: A KID WITH A TV
who.from: carrying a cracked TV out of the {raided} town

events.says: The {raider} already took the good stuff. They left the doors open. Everybody's in there taking what's left. There's a pharmacy nobody found yet, jefe. You want in?

opts.t: Go in and take what's left.

fx.say: Fourteen in cells and two cans. A woman in a doorway watches you carry it out.

opts.t: Tell him to put it back.

fx.say: Put it back for who? For the {raider}? They'll be back next week for the TV.
Okay. More for me.

who.name: A MAN WITH A WALKMAN
who.from: holding a cassette he pulled off a fence

events.says: Listen to this. Somebody tapes cassettes to the fences. Same voice every time, reading the price of eggs. Every week the price is higher. This one says a dozen eggs, one hundred ninety dollars. Dollars, bro. Who is still counting in dollars?

fx.say: After the eggs, milk. After the milk, ten seconds of a crowd breathing. Then the date, and it is next week.
Two. Keep it. I don't want it in my house anymore.
Yeah. Don't listen. That's what I should've done.

who.name: A MOTHER UNDER A SIGN
who.from: under a digital billboard flickering on a dying solar cell

events.says: It comes on every night at the same time. BUFFET, NINE NINETY-NINE. Somebody still pays for the cell. My boy watches it for the food. He thinks if he watches long enough they open.

opts.t: Give the boy a night of food.

fx.say: He eats it looking at the sign. He says it tastes like nine ninety-nine.

opts.t: Pull the cell out of the sign.

fx.say: Six in the cell. The sign goes dark. The boy doesn't cry. He just keeps looking at it.
It's okay. It comes on again tomorrow.

who.name: A MAN WITH A LEDGER
who.from: a pressed shirt, a ledger, two big men behind him

events.says: Your crew owes. Not you. One of your men signed for a loan with the Mob before he walked with you. Forty batteries and the interest. A debt doesn't care who you work for now. Pay half today and we write it closed, or we take him.

fx.say: Closed. Clean. I'll write your name in the good column.
Sensible. He'll work it off. They always do, eventually.

opts.t: Walk on. He can find you.

fx.say: We always do. It's sixty next time. The ledger doesn't sleep.

who.name: PADRE ANSELMO
who.from: ringing a hand bell at a crossroads in the dark

events.says: I ring it for the ones in the houses who died alone after the money went. Nobody came for them, so I come. Every night a different street. Tonight it's this one. Stand with me a minute, hijo, it's only a minute.

fx.say: Thirty-one doors. He says each number out loud. Nobody opens one.

opts.t: Give him a battery for candles.

fx.say: One candle a house. That's tonight's street. Gracias.
Go with God. Somebody will ring for you too.

who.name: THE WATER MAN
who.from: a tanker truck painted with a wave, a hose and a line of jugs

events.says: Agua del lago! Lake Mead, the deep intake, the third straw. Boiled twice. Three batteries a jug. Food and water is the same thing out here, compa, you know that.

fx.say: Two jugs. Drink the old one first, the new one keeps.
Lower every year. The first straw sucks air since 2022, the second since 2027. The third is the last one. After that we drink the river, and the river is Arizona's.
Okay. The sun will sell it to you later, more expensive.

who.name: {man}
who.from: at the battery box, at the night stop

events.head: IN THE COMPANY
events.says: Boss, the battery box is light. Six short. I counted twice. It was me. My sister in Henderson has a boy on an oxygen machine, and the machine eats batteries. I was going to tell you.

opts.t: Let the batteries go. It is a kid.

fx.say: {man} sends them south with the next cart. No thank you. None needed.

yes.say: {man} pays it back over a week and never says another word about it.

no.say: In the morning {man}'s bedroll is gone, and six more batteries with it.

fx.say: {man} goes with nothing but the clothes on. Four of the six are still in the bedroll.

who.name: {man}
who.from: at the wagon, in the morning

events.head: IN THE COMPANY
events.says: Six of the cans from the last town are swelling at the ends. My grandmother said a can that swells will kill you, and she lived through the last time the money went bad.

fx.say: Three nights of food into a ditch. Nobody gets sick.

opts.t: Boil them hard for ten minutes and eat them.

yes.say: Boiled long and eaten fast. Boiling kills the poison, the cook says. Nobody gets sick, and the food is kept.

no.say: {man} is sick all night: the cramps, then the double vision. {man} will be weak for days.

yes.say: They taste like tin. Nobody gets sick, this time.

no.say: By morning {man} cannot stand up straight. It will be days before {man} can fight.

who.name: {man}
who.from: looking down a dead road

events.head: IN THE COMPANY
events.says: See that road? I drove it every day, to {place}. Nobody has been in there since the lights went. I know the side door and where they kept the keys. It is about {blocks} blocks from here.

opts.t: Mark it on the map. We will go there.

fx.say: {man} draws it in the dirt for everybody: the side door, the loading dock, the bend in the road. {place} is on your map now.
{man} looks down the road a while longer, then picks up the pack.

who.name: {man}
who.from: at the water cans, before dawn

events.head: IN THE COMPANY
events.says: {other} drank the last of the water in the night, boss, my share too. I am going to break {other}'s face unless you tell me why I should not.

opts.t: Split two nights of water between everybody.

fx.say: Everybody drinks. Nobody fights. The cans stay full another day.
It is over in a minute. {other} has a split lip and a rib that hurts to breathe on for a few days.

who.name: {man}
who.from: at the fire, with a letter

events.head: IN THE COMPANY
events.says: A man came through from Pahrump. My mother and my two sisters are still out there. He says the wells went dry on their street and the ranch stopped selling to them. I have to go to them, boss. Or I have to send them something.

opts.t: Go. Take two nights of food for the road.

fx.say: {man} shakes every hand in the company and walks west at first light.

opts.t: Send them five batteries with the next cart.

fx.say: Five batteries go west with a cart driver {man} trusts. {man} stays.

opts.t: Say the company needs every hand.

yes.say: {man} stays, and does not sleep much.

no.say: In the morning {man}'s bedroll is gone, and five batteries with it.

who.name: THE PLASMA VAN
who.from: a van with a generator, by the road

events.says: Four batteries a pint, paid on the cot. We test you first. The hospitals on the Strip buy everything we take. {man} there looks healthy. Up and walking again by tomorrow.

fx.say: An hour on a cot. {man} comes back pale and four batteries heavier, and will be slow for a day.
The man in the van shrugs. There is a line behind you.

who.name: A WOMAN ON HER STEP
who.from: outside a house on a cul-de-sac

events.says: The bank sold the whole street to a man with a crew, and the crew collects rent in batteries now. Three a week. I paid it for three years. This week I do not have it, so they are taking the door off.

fx.say: The crew counts the three twice and puts the door back on. The street saw you do it.

win.say: Their week's take, six batteries, and the door stays on.

lose.say: They took her rent out of your pocket instead.

fx.say: The door comes off behind you.

who.name: A MAN WITH A BUCKET
who.from: at a foreclosed house with a green pool

events.says: Every house on this street was foreclosed in the first crash, and nobody ever drained the pools. Now they are the only water for a mile. Green, full of mosquitoes. You can have some if you carry it.

opts.t: Boil two nights of it for the wagon.

fx.say: Two hours over a fire made of a fence. It tastes like the bottom of a pool. It is water.

opts.t: Fill up and drink it as it is.

no.say: {man} is burning up by night. The mosquitoes, or the water.

who.name: A MAN ON A LADDER
who.from: at the top of a streetlight

events.says: There is copper wire in every one of these poles, and copper trades for batteries at the scrap yard. The lights have not been on in years. Help me strip the block and we split it.

fx.say: Three hours of wire, four batteries at the scrap yard. The street is darker than it was, and the people on it know who did it.

opts.t: Tell him to leave the poles alone.

fx.say: He climbs down and spits. Somebody on the corner nods at you.

who.name: A MAN IN A POLO SHIRT
who.from: outside a resort with no roof

events.says: Folks! Ninety minutes of your time and breakfast is on us. Real eggs: we keep chickens on the roof now. Vacation ownership is still the smartest money in Nevada. Ask me about week thirty-two.

opts.t: Sit through the pitch for the breakfast.

fx.say: Ninety minutes that take two hours. The eggs are real. He shakes every hand twice.
He hands you the deed to week thirty-two of room 1411. The room has no wall on one side. He calls it the view.
He calls after you that the offer ends today. It has ended today for eleven years.

who.name: A WOMAN WITH A SIGN
who.from: on the picket line outside a casino

events.says: The casino pays us in its own chips now. Good at its buffet and its store and nowhere else, and the buffet doubled its prices. So we stopped working. Do not cross the line. If you have food, we are on day nineteen.

opts.t: Give the line two nights of food.

fx.say: They pass it down the line. Somebody writes your company's name on a sign.

opts.t: Cross the line and sell to the casino.

fx.say: The casino's store pays well for what you carry. On the way out, nobody on the line looks at you.
Day nineteen. She turns back to the line.

who.name: A WOMAN AT A BANK MACHINE
who.from: on a dead corner

events.says: It still has power. A battery inside it, I think. Every morning I put my card in and it says my balance is zero, and every morning I believe it a little less. Open it if you want. I only want to see it say something else.

fx.say: Inside: forty thousand in twenties and the machine's own battery, still good. You take the battery. The screen goes dark in the middle of a word.
Behind you the machine asks her if she would like a receipt.

who.name: A WOMAN WITH TWO KIDS
who.from: on the road out of {home}

events.head: FOR YOUR PLACE
events.says: We lost the house in the first year of the crash and the car in the second. People say you have walls at {home}. I can cook for twenty and keep a ledger. The kids carry water. We do not need much, only a door that locks.

home.name: THE WIDOW AND HER TWO
home.says: She keeps the ledger. The kids carry the water up before anybody else is awake.

fx.say: Two nights of food for the walk, and a door at {home}. She asks where the ledger is before she asks where she sleeps.

opts.t: Give them two nights of food and point them to the shelter.

fx.say: She counts the food twice and thanks you once. The kids are already walking.

who.name: A MAN WITH A SHOPPING CART
who.from: pushing a solar panel down the middle of the road

events.head: FOR YOUR PLACE
events.says: Pulled it off a foreclosed roof in Summerlin, the bank's notice still taped to the door. A panel lasts thirty years and this one has twenty left in it. I will walk it all the way to {home} myself.

opts.t: Pay him ten batteries for the panel.

fx.say: He pushes the cart toward {home} without being asked twice. The bank's notice is still stuck to the back of the panel.

opts.t: Trade him four nights of food for it.

fx.say: Food, not batteries: he eats the first can before he lets go of the cart.

who.name: A WATER HAULER
who.from: with a tank on a trailer and no truck

events.head: FOR YOUR PLACE
events.says: The water district lost its pressure above the second floor everywhere west of Rainbow. A tank on a roof is water for a month. I pulled this one four miles by hand and I cannot pull it one more block.

fx.say: Six batteries and a handshake. He shows you how to bleed the air out of the line before he goes.

opts.t: Help him pull it to the next town for a share.

fx.say: Three hours of pulling. He sells the water by the bucket at {town} and pays you three batteries out of the first bucket.

who.name: A LIBRARIAN
who.from: with a card catalogue drawer full of seed packets

events.head: FOR YOUR PLACE
events.says: The library lent seeds before it stopped lending books. Squash, tepary beans, chiles, the ones that take the heat. The rule was you bring back seeds from what you grow. Nobody has brought any back.

opts.t: Take a drawer of seeds for a garden at {home}.

fx.say: Three batteries for the library, she says, and writes your name on the card in pencil. Due back next year.

opts.t: Carry the catalogue to the next town for her.

fx.say: Two hours with a drawer under each arm. At {town} she sets the catalogue on a table and opens for business.

who.name: A MAN WHO RAN FROM {boss}
who.from: hiding in a drainage ditch

events.head: ABOUT {boss}
events.says: I worked for {boss} at {boss_place}. Everybody does, or they leave the valley. I know the way in and where the men sleep. I want food and to be far from here before anybody knows I talked.

opts.t: Give him two nights of food for the way in.

fx.say: He draws it in the dirt with a stick: the gate, the yard, the room where {boss} sleeps. Then he is gone up the wash.

opts.t: Give him five batteries to get out of the valley.

fx.say: Five batteries buys a seat on a cart to Barstow. He tells you everything about {boss_place} on the way to the cart.

opts.t: Hand him back to the men of {boss} for the reward.

fx.say: Four batteries. Nobody in {town} will look at you the same way, and the man does not look at you at all.

who.name: A MAN SELLING MAPS
who.from: with a roll of county maps under his arm

events.head: ABOUT {boss}
events.says: The county assessor's maps, every parcel in the valley, printed the week before the servers went dark. I marked where {boss} sits. It is about {boss_blocks} blocks from here. Paper does not need a signal.

opts.t: Buy the map for four batteries.

fx.say: Parcel numbers, lot lines, and a red circle around {boss_place} in ballpoint.

opts.t: Trade him two hours of carrying for it.

fx.say: Two hours hauling his rolls of paper to {town}. He pays with the map that has the red circle on it.

who.name: THE MEN OF {boss}
who.from: at a roadblock of shopping carts and tires

events.head: ABOUT {boss}
events.says: This road belongs to {boss} from here to {boss_place}. Everybody pays to use it. Four batteries for the lot of you, or turn around and go the long way.

fx.say: They roll one cart out of the way and roll it back behind you.
Two and a half hours around through the washes. Their fire is still burning when you look back.

win.say: The carts go into the ditch and the tolls in their can go into your wagon.

lose.say: They take the toll anyway, and more for the trouble.

who.name: A MAN WHO FOUGHT FOR {boss}
who.from: on the curb with his rifle across his knees

events.head: ABOUT {boss}
events.says: {boss} is dead and the rest of us have nobody to pay us. I can shoot and I know every room of {boss_place}. Feed me and I will shoot for you instead.

fx.say: Three nights of food up front. He hands you the rifle to hold while he eats, and asks for it back after.

opts.t: Pay him to take the rest of them out of the valley.

fx.say: Six batteries. By morning eleven men are walking north on the 95 with their rifles slung, and the street is quiet.

who.name: A RUNNER FROM {job_from}
who.from: out of breath on the shoulder

events.head: ABOUT YOUR JOB
events.says: {job_from} sent me about your job: {job}. They need it sooner than you said. If you push, they will remember it. If you do not, they will remember that too.

fx.say: Extra rations to keep the men on their feet. The runner goes back to {job_from} with the word that you are coming.

opts.t: Tell them it takes what it takes.

fx.say: The runner writes it down word for word. {job_from} will read it out loud, he says.

who.name: A CREW BOSS ON A MOTORBIKE
who.from: idling across the road

events.head: ABOUT YOUR JOB
events.says: Heard {job_from} gave you their job: {job}. They gave it to us first, before you came along. Walk away and nobody gets hurt. Or pay us to walk away. Your call.

fx.say: Four batteries in his saddlebag. The motorbike goes the other way, and so does his crew.

win.say: They leave the motorbike's battery behind. {job_from} hears who kept their job.

lose.say: They take four batteries and laugh about it. The job is still yours, if you can still do it.

who.name: A KID ON A ROOF
who.from: waving from a carport

events.head: ABOUT YOUR JOB
events.says: There are men waiting at the underpass for whoever comes through on business for {job_from}. They have been there since morning. Two batteries and I show you the long way around.

opts.t: Pay the kid and go the long way.

fx.say: Two hours of back yards and broken fences. You never see the underpass.

yes.say: Nobody at the underpass but a burned-out car. The kid was lying, or they got bored.

no.say: A shot from the dark at the far end. {man} is hit in the arm before you are through.

who.name: AN OLD MAN AT A BUS STOP
who.from: at a bus stop with no buses

events.head: ABOUT YOUR JOB
events.says: You are working for {job_from}? My daughter lives there. I have not heard from her since the phones went. Take this letter to her. Her name is on it.

fx.say: Half an hour while he writes one more line at the bottom. {job_from} will know who brought it.
He puts the letter back in his coat and keeps waiting for the bus.

who.name: THE PEOPLE {boss} KEPT
who.from: walking out of {boss_place} with nothing

events.head: AFTER {boss}
events.says: We cooked for {boss} for two years at {boss_place}, for nothing, because the door was locked from his side. Now it is open and we do not know where to go. Somebody said you have a place.

opts.t: Feed them and send them to your place.

home.name: THE COOKS OF {boss_place}
home.says: They cook for everybody now, and nobody locks the door.

fx.say: Three nights of food for the walk. They go toward your place singing something from before.

opts.t: Give them two nights of food for the road.

fx.say: They split it six ways and thank you six times. By tonight {town} knows who opened the door.

who.name: THE BROTHER OF {boss}
who.from: waiting in the middle of the road

events.head: AFTER {boss}
events.says: You put {boss} down. He was a bad man and he was my brother. I am not here to forgive it. Pay what his life was worth to his mother, or we settle it here.

fx.say: He counts them twice and walks away without a word. The road is quiet after.

win.say: It is over. His rifle had two batteries taped to the stock.

lose.say: He takes the six batteries anyway, and leaves you lying in the road.

who.name: A MAN WITH A STRONGBOX
who.from: sitting on a strongbox at the roadside

events.head: AFTER {boss}
events.says: This is what {boss} took from every stall in {town}, every week, for years. I carried it out of {boss_place} after he fell. It is not mine. It is not yours either. Tell me what to do with it.

opts.t: Carry it back to the stalls.

fx.say: An hour and a half, stall by stall, back to who it came from. Nobody in {town} will forget it.
Six batteries in the box. The man walks off. In {town} they say you took over where {boss} stopped.

who.name: A SQUATTER
who.from: on the steps of {boss_place}

events.head: AFTER {boss}
events.says: {boss_place} is empty since you put {boss} down. People are already fighting over who moves in. Whoever has the sign off the door is the one people listen to. That could be you.

opts.t: Take the sign off the door for your place.

home.name: THE SIGN OF {boss_place}
home.says: It hung over the door of {boss_place} until {boss} fell.

fx.say: Two hours with a crowbar. The sign goes on the cart to your place, and the squatters stop arguing.

opts.t: Burn it so nobody takes his place.

fx.say: An hour to get it burning. The smoke from {boss_place} shows from {town}, and people come out to watch it go.

who.name: A MAN FROM {deed_town}
who.from: on the shoulder with his arms crossed

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: You took our job in {deed_town} and you did not finish it. We gave food up front to the crew we trusted, and we went hungry for it. People there say your name now the way they say a curse.

fx.say: He takes them to {deed_town}. It does not make it right, he says, but it is something they will remember.

opts.t: Tell him it did not work out.

fx.say: He spits on the road and walks back toward {deed_town}.

who.name: A WOMAN WITH A BANDAGED ARM
who.from: by a fire on the road out of {deed_town}

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: Nobody came to {deed_town} when you said you would. The men you were paid to stop came instead. My husband is in the ground and my arm will not close. I am not asking you for anything. I wanted you to see it.

opts.t: Give her three nights of food.

fx.say: She takes it without looking at you. It is the only thing you can do here.
She watches you go. Someone from {deed_town} is watching too.

who.name: THE ELDER OF {deed_town}
who.from: on a mule at the crossroads

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: The job in {deed_town} went bad. It happens to everybody once. There is a smaller one: the pump on the east side needs a crew to sit on it for four hours tonight. Do it, and we will talk to you again.

opts.t: Sit on the pump for four hours.

fx.say: Four quiet hours on the pump. Three batteries and a nod from the elder. {deed_town} will talk to you again.
The elder turns the mule around without a word.

who.name: A KID WITH A GUITAR
who.from: on a bus bench, singing

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: There is a song in {deed_town} about the crew that took the job and never came. Everybody knows the words. I can sing it for you. Or you can pay me not to sing it anywhere else.

opts.t: Pay him two batteries to stop.

fx.say: He pockets the batteries and starts another song, about something else.
He sings it all the way through. It is a good song. {town} will be singing it by tonight.

who.name: A WOMAN FROM {deed_town}
who.from: walking out to meet the cart

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: You did right by {deed_town}. People there will not say it to your face, so I came out to say it. And I brought this: bread from the oven behind the church, and peppers.

fx.say: Four nights of bread and peppers. She waves the whole way back to {deed_town}.

opts.t: Tell her to give it to the shelter.

fx.say: She looks at you a long time and nods. {deed_town} will hear that too.

who.name: A YOUNG MAN FROM {deed_town}
who.from: with a rifle and a bedroll

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: I saw what your crew did for {deed_town}. I want to do that. I can shoot, I can carry, and I do not complain. My mother says I am too young. She is wrong.

fx.say: Two nights of food up front. He shakes everybody's hand, twice.

opts.t: Send him back to guard his town.

fx.say: He argues, then goes. His mother will hear who sent him home.

who.name: A RUNNER FROM {deed_town}
who.from: out of breath in the road

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: {deed_town} sent me after you. There are men at the next overpass waiting for whoever comes this way. We owe you, so we are telling you.

fx.say: An hour and a half the long way. From the hill you see them under the overpass, still waiting.

yes.say: They see you coming ready and let you pass. Nobody wants that fight.

no.say: A shot from under the overpass. {man} takes it in the shoulder, and then they run.

who.name: A TRADER WHO HEARD
who.from: with a mule loaded with sacks

events.head: AFTER THE JOB
events.says: Word from {deed_town} is that you keep your word. That is worth something to me. I will sell you food cheap today, or buy yours at a fair price. Most people I would cheat.

opts.t: Buy five nights of food for three batteries.

fx.say: Five nights of beans and rice off the mule, for three batteries.

opts.t: Sell him four nights of food for four batteries.

fx.say: Four batteries, counted out on the mule's back.
